patch.stem: An Azure SDK client has automatic retries disabled. Its get_status operation is an idempotent read. The service returns HTTP 429 with Retry-After expressed in seconds. The caller supplies a finite remaining_retry_budget_seconds. Complete this handler: retry at most once, honor the full server delay, and propagate other failures.
patch.explanation: The decisive clue is the server-provided minimum delay. HttpResponseError exposes the HTTP status; only 429 enters this throttle handler. Retry-After specifies seconds under this exercise’s contract. Sleep for the entire delay when the remaining budget permits it; otherwise propagate the failure so the caller can defer. A 30-second cap could retry early. Non-429 errors, invalid delay values and failures of the single retry propagate. HTTP-date headers would require a date parser in a different service contract.
patch.decisionRule: A retry budget decides whether to retry; it never shortens Retry-After.
patch.takeaway: A retry budget decides whether to retry; it never shortens Retry-After.
